problem: Realistic PointNav (RGB-D and actuation noise, no GPS+Compass) remained far from solved: the best published result was 71.7% Success, and it was unclear whether an explicit map is needed to navigate under these conditions.
motivation: Whether explicit mapping is necessary for navigation is a scientific question with roots in animal cognition and in classical robotics. Under idealized settings map-less RL agents already reach 100% Success, so the realistic setting is the open test. The authors observe that with ground-truth GPS+Compass, noise in sensing and actuation barely matters, which points to localization (visual odometry) as the bottleneck.
key_idea: Train a map-less RL navigation policy with ground-truth localization, then swap in a much stronger visual odometry module (action embeddings, flip/swap augmentation at train and test time, and 5M pairs with a ResNet50) to close the realistic-setting gap.
insight: With GT localization the policy reaches 99.8% Success under full sensor and actuation noise, so the only bottleneck is odometry (Table 1, row 17). VO gains come from cheap ingredients: action embeddings (+7 Success), Flip augmentation, test-time augmentation ensembling, and scale (500k to 5M pairs, ResNet18 to ResNet50, taking Success from 64 to 96). Augmentations help more with more data (test-time +3 Success at 0.5M vs +5 at 1.5M). Swap augmentation hurts alone and helps only combined with Flip. However, VO transfers poorly across datasets (Gibson to MP3D drops Success 96.0 to 79.4).
method: Decoupled agent: a DD-PPO navigation policy (half-width ResNet50 + 2-layer LSTM, depth only, GT GPS+Compass at training) is trained first. At test time GT localization is replaced by VO estimates that update the goal vector each step, with no fine-tuning.

Visual odometry network: ResNet encoder (half width, GroupNorm) on channel-stacked RGB-D pairs, followed by a 3x3 conv compression block and 2 FC layers with dropout 0.2. It regresses (dx,dy,dz,dtheta) with MSE.
Action embedding: a fixed 16-d vector per action is concatenated to the encoder output and to the input of all FC layers (no dropout on it).
Train-time augmentations: Swap (swap the frame order and invert the rotation action and pose, for rotation actions only) and the new Flip (mirror both frames and negate dx and dtheta).
Test-time augmentation ensembling: run VO on the flipped/swapped variants (2 pairs for forward, 4 for rotations), map predictions back with the inverse transforms, and average.
Scaling: VO dataset grown from 0.5M to 1.5M to 5M pairs, ResNet18 to ResNet50, with distributed VO training on 64 GPUs (about 5,000 GPU hours). Policy trained for 7.5B steps in 3 stages.
Oracle upper bound: a heuristic planner using the GT map and motion primitives reaches 84% SPL, showing that 100% SPL is not attainable under noisy actuation.

setting.backbone: DD-PPO policy (half-width ResNet50 + 2-layer LSTM) plus visual odometry CNN (ResNet18/ResNet50, trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Policy: Gibson full train via RL, 7.5B steps. VO: 0.5M to 5M RGB-D pairs with GT egomotion, sampled from oracle trajectories on Gibson 4+ scenes. Sim2real used Gibson, MP3D and HM3D.
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB-D (noise models: Gaussian for RGB, Redwood for depth); policy uses depth only; no GPS+Compass
setting.action_space: Discrete: STOP, FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30° (noisy actuation, no sliding)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT GPS+Compass and the GT-map oracle are used only for analysis rows)

numbers.eval_set_note: Habitat Challenge 2021 PointNav test-std split (realistic PointNav-v2)
numbers.backbone: DD-PPO policy + ResNet50 VO (5M pairs, flip/swap TTA)

numbers_note: MP3D VO fine-tuning result (85.6 Success / 65.9 SPL) appears only in the supplementary text and is not listed. Sim2real: 9 episodes, 11% Success, 65% SoftSPL, 92% SoftSuccess. DTG on MP3D is printed on a different scale (x10^2 cm-like) as given.
results: On the Habitat Challenge 2021 PointNav test-std split the agent reaches 94% Success / 74% SPL, versus 78/59 for the prior published VO2021 (Zhao et al.) and 91/70 for the concurrent unpublished inspir.ai. Val ablations improve Success from 64% to 96%, close to the 99.8% obtained with GT odometry.
limitations: VO is embodiment-specific (relies on action embeddings) and dataset-specific: Success drops from 96.0 to 79.4 when moving from Gibson to MP3D.
Very high compute: 7.5B policy steps and about 5,000 GPU hours for VO.
Sim2real is very preliminary (9 episodes, 11% Success), and the paper studies only the direct mapping-to-navigation link, not indirect links via localization.
builds_on: Zhao et al. 2021 VO for realistic PointNav
